note: Two schemes, and the reason there are two: a system that only works in
one palette is not finished. These are the two the field's own preview
puts side by side — the committed mauve scheme and an amber one from
another wallpaper — and the system's guarantees are checked against both.
A scheme says what it changes and leaves the rest alone. A role the
scheme does not mention keeps the system's own value, so a consumer
that carries a scheme for one role still has the system's other roles,
and the guarantees are checked against the whole and not against the
part.
The state grounds travel with the ink. A scheme that changes the ink
changes the ground the ink is written on, or the pairing breaks — the
green the system declares is not dark enough to carry a light ink, and
the audit is what says so. That is why these two carry a positive
surface of their own.
The mapping from the field's Material 3 roles to the system's roles is:
layer0 to the surface, layer1 to the sunken ground, layer2 to the
overlay, layer3 to the raised ground, the primary to the accent, the
on-primary to the accent's ink, the on-surface to the ink and the
on-surface-variant to the muted ink. The mapping is the field's; the
guarantees are the system's, and the audit measures them.
The light substrate is not carried by these two schemes: the field's
shell forces the dark one, so the light half of a dynamic scheme is
written and never read. The system keeps its own light values there,
and that is a known gap rather than a decision.
